A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DARE research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Taobao/Tmall experiments, attention and representation analyses, Amazon and Shakespeare experiments, and a five-day online A/B test.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds comparison variants, sensitivity studies, gradient analyses, and GAUC/Logloss evaluations in Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: DARE retains its separate attention and representation embeddings, top-K retrieval, scaled dot-product attention, and target-aware representation aggregation. The additional decoupling designs are experimental comparators, not changes to the final DARE procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Taobao, Tmall, Amazon, Shakespeare, and the same online advertising study. Naming Tencent does not introduce another deployment scenario. The Amazon experiment moves from Section 4.7 to Appendix D.2; sequence-length sweeps vary settings within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C/Table 3 adds seven evaluated alternatives: item-only, category-only, time-only, and category-plus-time projections; larger-embedding projection; MLP projection; and gradient-norm balancing. The existing linear-projection variant and main Table 1 comparator set are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds category-grouped GAUC and Logloss evaluation, retrieval-count sweeps from 1 to 25, history-length sweeps, joint attention/representation dimension sweeps, and category-wise gradient-monitoring procedures. The existing data splits and default training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C–E substantially expand mechanism and sensitivity analyses: alternative decoupling strategies, MLP optimization behavior, retrieval count, history length, embedding dimensions, and conflict versus category frequency. Conversely, v1's Figure 5 attention-logit distribution analysis is removed. Existing attention and retrieval case studies are retained and regrouped.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations; the new tables extend that existing practice. Neither version specifies run counts or seeds, and v2 introduces no confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: The main AUC table, Amazon scores, and online lifts are unchanged, but v2 adds extensive variant, sensitivity, GAUC, Logloss, and gradient-conflict results. The additional metrics reveal different rankings: at dimension 16 on Taobao, Logloss is 0.61922 for DARE, versus 0.35402 for SDIM and 0.37096 for TWIN-V2. These are newly reported comparisons, not performance changes between versions.

T1.justification: Appendix E.3 adds an explicit MI definition containing log[p(x)p(y)/p(x,y)], reversing the standard log ratio. This introduces a mathematical documentation error absent from v1, without establishing a changed empirical calculation. The DARE equations and assumptions otherwise remain equivalent; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the failure claim from linear projections to common decoupling methods and introduce a claimed first analysis through multi-task learning. The central DARE contribution and headline AUC, online GMV, and search-acceleration claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial interpretations concerning residual gradient conflict, MLP optimization difficulty, conditions under which retrieval and longer histories favor DARE, and the relative importance of representation dimensions. Appendix E.1 attributes SDIM/TWIN-V2's lower Logloss to conservative predictions, while E.2 interprets category-frequency results as evidence of widespread conflict. The limitations also acknowledge one-stage alternatives.

D1.justification: v2 reports release of PyTorch code for preprocessing, training, and analysis, supplies an access link and reproducibility statement, identifies the deployment platform as Tencent, and states that MI probabilities are estimated from training data. Existing optimizer, hyperparameters, baseline adaptations, and data-split instructions are largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds multi-task-learning positioning through Caruana, gradient surgery, and conflict-averse gradient descent references, plus the one-stage IFA reference. The established recommendation literature remains central. Publication-year and venue updates to existing references do not constitute additional cited works.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites in the abstract, introduction, and gradient-analysis discussion. Section 4.7 becomes an appendix-results overview, the Amazon discussion moves to Appendix D.2, and reproducibility and acknowledgement sections are added. The main six-section narrative remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 12–18 and Tables 3–5, redraws and color-codes the DARE architecture, and removes v1's attention-logit histogram. Previously unnumbered appendix heatmaps and retrieval cases are consolidated into Figures 19–20. These are substantial display additions and reorganizations beyond routine renumbering.

improvement.justification: The additional comparison and sensitivity studies strengthen the empirical justification for decoupling and clarify its useful operating range; reported code access improves reproducibility. These benefits are tempered by new reporting problems: Table 3 gives the Tmall linear-projection gain as 0.00988 instead of 0.00340, Appendix E.3 reverses the MI log ratio, and Section 4.7 claims consistent superiority despite Table 5's Logloss exceptions. The net improvement is therefore limited.
